newsitem.title: BURMA: Burmese students stage rare protest against SLORC.
newsitem.headline: Burmese students stage rare protest against SLORC.

text.p: About 500 Burmese university students on Wednesday staged a rare demonstration against the military government and its handling of a recent scuffle involving students at a food stall, witnesses said.

The three-hour demonstration at an intersection about two km (1.2 miles) from the house of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi ended after teachers from the Yangon Institute of Technology and education ministry officials persuaded the students to disperse.

The government said on Wednesday it had not arrested any of the students involved in the protest. But a diplomat said he had heard some of the students who did not want to go home were escorted by heavily armed security police.
The students said they were protesting against the detention of three classmates who were involved in an argument at a food stall on Sunday. The three were detained briefly by police.
A similar quarrel at a tea shop in 1988 sparked nationwide outrage against the military government, leading to pro-democracy street demonstrations that left thousands dead or in jail.

The students involved in the protest on Wednesday said government-run television and radio broadcasts on Tuesday night on the detention of the three students were inaccurate and failed to say the police had manhandled the detainees.

The demonstrators demanded an apology from the police within 48 hours and said they wanted the government to broadcast a correct chronology of the events leading to the detention and the release of the students.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) issued a statement calling the demands impossible and said the students were trying to instigate unrest.
"If we study the chronology of this incident, it can be found that a restaurant quarrel was forged and diverted to become public unrest," said the statement.
It accused the students of colluding with Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) party and said they and politicians were trying to turn the quarrel into a bigger political issue.
"The students' unrest was mixed with politics on purpose to make the matter worse," the statement said.

"Members of the security forces had to control the situation by taking a preventative measure so as not to let peace be spoiled and in order to maintain community peace and tranquillity and the rule of law," it said.
No one from the group of demonstrating students or senior NLD officials was immediately available for comment.

Diplomats and NLD sources said deputy NLD chairman Kyi Maung, a close confidant of Suu Kyi, was detained for questioning late on Tuesday. He was singled out by the SLORC in its statement for meeting two of the students before the protest was held.
Witnesses said the SLORC again blocked access to Suu Kyi's University Avenue home on Tuesday night by closing off roads which had been reopened on Monday after being sealed for 10 days.
Suu Kyi's phone has been out of order since late September, when the government thwarted NLD plans to hold a September 27-29 party congress at her house.
At the time the government set up barricades manned by security police to prevent the meeting from taking place. The SLORC also arrested 573 activists to prevent unrest. They were later released.
